_comment2: Run: python3 w3_ai_scripts/gen_platformio.py  to regenerate platformio.ini
_core_dir_note: core_dir gives THIS TREE its own PlatformIO home instead of the shared ~/.platformio. It is required here and must not be removed while this branch is on a different Arduino/IDF than master. REASON: a git worktree separates TREES, NOT ENVIRONMENTS. pioarduino's platform.json declares name=espressif32 and its Arduino core installs to the same packages/framework-arduinoespressif32 path as the official platform, so the two OVERWRITE each other in a shared home -- whichever built last wins and the other breaks. Observed twice on 2026-09-03: a master build silently reinstalled Arduino 2.0.17 over 3.3.11 and broke this branch with FRAMEWORK_DIR=None; a branch build then broke master's ESP32 targets for other sessions. The version pin does NOT protect against this -- it selects the platform, it does not stop the platform from rewriting a shared package. Setting it HERE rather than exporting PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR per command is the point: an env var is a habit and one forgotten prefix re-contaminates the shared home, which is exactly how it happened the second time. UPDATED 2026-09-04: this note used to end 'Absent on master, which correctly keeps the default home' -- that is no longer true, because the migration merged (29ec1ff) and master IS pioarduino now. It is KEPT rather than removed: ~/.platformio still holds the Arduino 2.0.17 / IDF 4.4.7 toolchain untouched, so it remains the rollback path, and keeping the two homes separate means reverting master does not require re-downloading a toolchain. Remove core_dir only if that rollback is deliberately abandoned.

feature_flags._psram_note: -mfix-esp32-psram-cache-issue is NOT here and must not come back here: it is an ESP32-CLASSIC (LX6) flag for the rev<3 PSRAM cache erratum, and xtensa-esp32s3-elf does not have the option at all. It lived in this shared block until 2026-09-03, which meant all five S3 boards were passing a flag their compiler does not implement -- tolerated silently by the old GCC 8.4.0 toolchain, and an unrecognized -m option is an error on the GCC 15.x toolchain that comes with Arduino 3.x/IDF 5.x. It now sits in chip_flags on the two LX6 boards (Freenove-4WD-Car-Kit-ESP32, Freenove-ESP32-WROVER), which is where a chip-specific flag belongs and where it cannot leak onto an S3 board by being added to a shared feature.
feature_flags._glibc_compat_note: B274.  Each --wrap needs a MATCHING --undefined, and the pair must name a symbol src/ll_glibc_compat.cpp actually defines.  A --wrap with no --undefined links clean and does NOTHING (nothing references the object, so it is never pulled from the archive) -- the binary keeps its GLIBC_2.38 requirement and refuses to start on Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL 9, with no build-time signal at all.  An --undefined naming a symbol nobody defines fails at LINK, which is the safe direction.  The seven symbols this exists to remove, from objdump -T on the shipped binary: fmod fmodf __isoc23_fscanf __isoc23_sscanf __isoc23_strtol __isoc23_strtoll __isoc23_strtoul.  VERIFY WITH: objdump -T LambLisp.bin | grep GLIBC_2.3[89] -- it must print nothing.
feature_flags._demo_profile_note: P174/P175 SHARED DEMO PROFILE.  Both the MinGW/Windows proposal and the WebAssembly one need byte-for-byte the SAME exclusion set -- no sockets, no raw terminal, no native code generator -- and P175 says explicitly to factor it ONCE rather than let two proposals each carry a copy that can drift apart.  This is that one copy.  IT SETS ONLY THE THREE SWITCHES NOTHING ELSE SETS: modbus/profibus/profinet are excluded by simply NOT listing them in a board's `features`, not by a -DLL_MODBUS=0 here -- adding one would collide with the -DLL_MODBUS=1 a board that lists both would also get, and a macro redefinition is a warning you will scroll past, not an error.  Meaning of each: LL_NETWORK=0 removes the TCP client/server ports and the whole BSD socket surface; LL_TERMIOS=0 removes raw terminal mode so input is line-at-a-time stdio; LL_NCG=0 compiles out all three NCG backends (the bytecode interpreter is unaffected -- its arithmetic shims live in ll_vm_ncg_core.cpp, which is always compiled).

partitions.comment: Map flash_mb -> partition CSV.  ALL ENTRIES ARE llloader LAYOUTS (factory=llloader / ota_0=VM / storage=FS), NOT duplicate-app A/B.  A board gets a recovery root only if its table has a `factory` slot, and the A/B tables have none -- so an env on one cannot be given a loader at all, no matter what flash_loader does.  gen_platformio.py derives board_build.app_partition_name and board_upload.offset_address from the table, so an env does not restate them.  The non-OTA tables (partitions_4M/8M/32M.csv, _ota_trim) are kept for reference and for anything that deliberately wants A/B; nothing maps to them.
